newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DUTCH JOURNALIST WINS HUNGARY LIBEL SUIT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH JOURNALIST WINS HUNGARY LIBEL SUIT.

text.p: A former Hungarian government press adviser has lost a libel suit against a Dutch journalist who quoted him as describing many state radio journalists as "alcoholics and communists", the journalist said.

Stefan Bos, Central Europe correspondent for Belgian BRTN radio and television, the Voice of America and Deutsche Welle, said on Monday a Budapest court had turned down an appeal of a lower court ruling which rejected a five million forints claim for damages sought by Tom Kennedy.

Kennedy, press adviser to former prime minister Peter Boross, sued after Bos quoted him as saying 320 Hungarian Radio journalists would be sacked as "an action against the old establishment...most of them are alcoholics and communists."
The statement was published on the eve of the 1994 elections which toppled the centre-right coalition government in which Boross was prime minister.

"I am extremely pleased, not only for myself but I also hope it sets a precedent for other (Hungarian) journalists in the future because there was fear to interview officials and a fear to write critically about them," Bos said.
Kennedy could not be reached for comment.
